summary: The staleness half of the brief (plan parts A to E); the cancellation half is left out (see left_out). src/finder/preview.rs: a preview is cached with a stamp taken from its item's row, `PreviewStamp = (Option<SystemTime>, Option<u64>)`: the modification date and, for a file only, the size (`preview_stamp(entry)`; a folder's size is left out because `decorate` fills it in from the index later). `ensure_preview` returns only when the load in flight for the path, or else the cached preview, has the entry's stamp. Otherwise it starts a load; the old preview stays in the cache until the new one lands, and inserting the new task drops a load in flight for another stamp. The 256 cap keeps the requested path's entry (`retain`). New `forget_previews(cx)` clears the cache and the loads and calls `selection_changed`. New doc-hidden `preview_text_for_test`; `preview_match_for_test` follows the new value type. src/finder/mod.rs: `previews: HashMap<PathBuf, (PreviewStamp, Preview)>`, `preview_tasks: HashMap<PathBuf, (PreviewStamp, Task<()>)>`. `selection_changed` is now called at each reread's completion: always in `load_listing` (it was called only when `select` was found), in `reload_recents` when the list is replaced, and in `load_column` when the pane is the active one. The four appearance changes (the system-appearance observer, `toggle_appearance`, `set_appearance`, `adopt_settings`) and `nu_changed` use `forget_previews`. Refresh keeps its `previews.clear()` and is covered by the listing's completion. src/finder/list.rs: `load_children` calls `selection_changed` after rebuilding the rows. src/finder/explore.rs: `Explore` records the row's `modified`, and `ensure_explore` opens the file again when it differs. docs/manual.md: the sentence about files changed in place in "The window", a paragraph under "Previews and Quick Look", and one sentence in the Images row of the preview table.
changelog: A preview no longer goes on showing a file as it was before it changed. When another program saved a file, the list showed its new size and date a couple of seconds later, while the Preview Pane, the column view's preview, the gallery, and Quick Look kept the old contents beside them. A preview is now read again when its item comes back with another size or date: when its folder is read again, when a search runs again, and when Recents is read again. The old preview stays until the new one is ready, and text stays where you were reading it. Quick Look opens a changed PDF again at its first page, and its explore mode a changed file from its top level. Refresh (Cmd+R) and switching between light and dark no longer leave the Preview Pane, the column view's preview, and Quick Look on a spinner until you select another item. A file written over in place, which changes nothing about its folder, still shows as it was until you refresh, and a picture still shows as it was first drawn until fffinder is restarted.
behaviour_changes: In the Preview Pane, the column view's card, the gallery and Quick Look, the selected item's preview is read again when its row comes back with another size or date: after the 2-second look rereads the window's folder, a folder open in the list, or the column pane that holds the selection (tested for each, with a file saved under another name and renamed over the old one); after any other reread of those (Refresh, Show Hidden Files, a file operation here or in another tab); when a search runs again and its answer is shown (tested with a contents search); when Recents is read again and comes out another list (tested). Before, the old contents stayed beside the new size and date. Pictured: the pane (implementer) and the card of a file in the third column (review).

While the new preview is read the old one stays up, with no spinner frame, and plain text and code keep their scroll position (tested). That holds when more than 256 previews are cached and the others are let go (tested in review).

Refresh (Cmd+R, F5) no longer leaves the Preview Pane, the column view's card and Quick Look on a spinner until another item is selected. It shows the file as it is now even when its size and date are unchanged (tested for the pane and, in review, for the card of a file in a further column; pictured for the card and for Quick Look's window).

A change of appearance no longer leaves those three on a spinner: Toggle Light/Dark, Settings, the system's appearance changing with System chosen, or a change adopted from another tab or window. The preview is read again in the new colors, and one still being read in the old colors no longer lands in them (tested for the pane and, in review, for Quick Look over the list with the pane hidden; pictured for the card and for Quick Look).
Quick Look's explore mode opens a file again when its row's date has changed, from its top level, so the place gone into is lost (tested, where nu is installed).

Quick Look outside the gallery opens a PDF again, at its first page, when its row's date has changed; a reread that brings the same date leaves the page where it was (tested in review: page 2 of 2 stays through a reread, and becomes page 1 of 12 when a twelve-page document takes the file's place). `pdf_view` matches by path only, so the old pages stayed before. The gallery did this already.
A folder's "N items" preview is read again when the folder's row comes back with another date (review probe: +1 load after a file was added in the folder and the window's folder reread).

The same file is read once more when it shows as a result of a search by name and then in its folder, or the other way round: the index's date is in whole seconds, the folder's is not. The old preview stays meanwhile, so only the work is new (review probe: 1 load each way, 0 when the same search runs again). A contents search reads the disk's date, so its results share their previews with the folder.

Column view: after a pane's reread has moved the highlight to another file (selection by place in the list, an existing problem that column-pane-selection-by-path fixes), the card reads that file's preview instead of waiting for one forever.

Column view: a reread of the pane in use, or a change of appearance, with a folder selected there reads that folder's item count once, which the column view doesn't show (review probe: +1 the first time, 0 after). Clicking through folders reads none, as before.
A load in flight for an item's earlier state is dropped when the item is asked for with its new state. A change of `nu` behaves as before.
Tabs that don't show, and split view's other pane, read their own selected item's preview again when their folder is reread, like the tab that shows: each browser has its own previews.
left_out: Cancelling loads for items already passed (the plan's optional Follow-up 1, the "-and-cancel" half of the title). Holding an arrow key still starts one full load per item passed, and each runs to its end. The verifier split it off as optional; its design skips only loads that haven't begun, which helps only when the thread pool is saturated (one thread per core on Linux and Windows; on macOS GPUI hands background work to GCD's global queue, which adds threads while its threads block, by the implementer's reading of gpui-pre-apple-0.3.10/src/dispatcher.rs), and as specified it has a hole: ask for X, then Y, then X again before X's load has begun, and X is skipped and, outside the gallery, left on a spinner. What costs is a `nu` already running per item passed, which needs a way to stop a running `nu` (src/nushell.rs waits for the child on the background thread and kills it only at its timeout).

In-place edits (the plan's Follow-up 2), as the verifier says. A file written over in place keeps its row and so its preview until its folder changes or Refresh. The manual says so of the preview too.

Refresh only clears the cache, as the plan says ("keep its clear"); loads in flight are not dropped there. So a load that was already running when Refresh was pressed can land with what it read before, if the file was written over in place while it ran; pressing Refresh once more reads it. Dropping the loads there would start one load per press in the gallery, which asks with every frame, and a `nu`-backed load can't be stopped once started.

Pictures. An image that GPUI decodes (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, BMP, ICO, TIFF, SVG) is drawn with `img(path)`, which GPUI keeps by path for as long as the app runs, so its preview and its thumbnail show the first picture they read, after Refresh too (review picture -review-picture-saved.png: the caption has the new size and date under the old picture). thumbnail-memory keys both by path and date; the manual and this entry's last clause say what is true without it.
The verifier's plan asked for an entry in CHANGELOG.md; the guide forbids it, and the entry is in the commit message.
No test of `--features term`: nothing in src/term calls what changed and no signature changed (grepped by the implementer and in review).

The changelog and the manual claimed more than is true: a picture is not read again (GPUI keeps an image by its path), and the entry said "a preview" without exception. The changelog entry now ends with it, the commit message says why, and the manual's Images row says so. It is in that row, not in the new paragraph, so that thumbnail-memory, which rewrites the row, has to meet it.

Behaviour change 6 of the implementer's report (a changed PDF in Quick Look opens again at its first page) was claimed by reading only. It is true; there is now a test for it (quick_look_opens_a_pdf_again_once_it_has_changed), which also pins that a reread with the same date leaves the page alone, and the manual and the changelog entry say it.

The 256-entry cap's `retain` had no test. a_preview_is_read_again_when_its_file_comes_back_changed now reads 300 other previews before its second save and holds the scroll position against where it was (with `clear()` in its place the position goes back to the top).

The changelog names the column view's card and Quick Look for Refresh and for a change of appearance, and the tests had only the Preview Pane. refresh_reads_the_shown_preview_again now also refreshes with the card showing a file in a further column, and a_preview_is_colored_again_when_the_appearance_changes toggles the appearance with Quick Look open over the list and the pane hidden.
Commit message: "a search result has the index's date" is true of a search by name only (a contents search reads the disk's date), and the PDF and the picture were missing.

The three ways I thought this most likely to hurt a user, and what the code says.
(1) A preview read over and over: a stamp that never matches what was cached, or two askers with different stamps for one path, with the gallery asking every frame. Every asker passes the row's own entry: `selection_changed` and Quick Look take `primary_entry()` (the rows, or in the column view `column_selection()`), `select_in_column` the pane's entry, `render_gallery` `primary_entry()` or the first row; pane 0's entries are the rows'. Nothing but `decorate` rewrites an entry after it is listed, and only a folder's size, which the stamp leaves out (`is_dir` covers bundles too). Results of a search by name carry the index's size and whole-second date and results of a contents search a fresh stat, each the same from one answer to the next. The load counts above and the randomized run agree: no load without a change, and no hang.
(2) A preview that never arrives, or a stale one shown as current. A task replaced in the map or cleared from it is dropped before it can land (async-task closes it; its completion is never polled), so the completion's `preview_tasks.remove(path)` can only remove its own entry. Everything that empties the cache asks again: `forget_previews` itself, and Refresh through the listing it starts, whose completion now always asks (also in the Trash, Recents, sent results and during a search, where the search's answer asks once more). All four surfaces draw `primary_entry()`, which is what `selection_changed` asks for, gated by the view, the pane or Quick Look being there; a surface that comes later asks when it comes (toggle_preview_pane, set_view_mode, Quick Look opening). "A load in flight decides alone" (the implementer's deviation 4) is the better rule: with the plan's rule a row that goes S, S', S while S' is being read keeps what S' read, stamped S', until something asks again, which outside the gallery may be never.
(3) Work, or a lost place, for a file that keeps changing. A reread happens at most every 2 seconds per folder (one look at a time, `checking_folders`), so a selected file that changes at every look is read every 2 seconds: nothing for text, one `nu` each time for a database or spreadsheet. A dropped load's `nu` can't be stopped, so a file whose `nu` preview takes longer than the 2 seconds keeps its old preview until the changes pause, with up to five `nu` running (10-second timeout). Explore mode and a PDF in Quick Look start over at each change of date, by the plan. I left these as they are; before, such a file was never read again.

Doubts that remain.
1. Only Linux was built and run. Nothing platform-specific changed.
2. The corner under (3). A rule that lets the load in flight finish and asks again when it lands would bound it to one `nu` and always show something newer; it is not what the verified plan says, and I did not change the design for a case I could not produce here.
3. previews_show_what_other_programs_save depends on a folder's change time differing between the fixture's creation and the test's save, like folders_on_screen_show_what_other_programs_add. The gap is the window opening, tens of milliseconds at least.
4. The cap phase reads 300 one-byte files; each landing redraws the window, about 2 seconds of the test here.
5. column-pane-selection-by-path (lane-f) and thumbnail-memory (lane-e) were committed in their lanes and not on the trunk when this went in. Both touch lines this change touches; see below.

For briefs still to come.
- column-pane-selection-by-path: you will conflict in two places. In `load_column`'s completion keep `if col == this.active_column { this.selection_changed(cx); }` after your remap and truncate, before `cx.notify()`: it reads `column_selection()`, which is by then the item you kept, and when `select_in_column_quiet` has just asked for the same entry it does nothing. In `load_listing` keep your `select_row_in_columns(first, cx)` inside the `if let Some((&first, rest))` block and `this.selection_changed(cx)` after the block, where it now stands for what stays selected too. previews_show_what_other_programs_save and refresh_reads_the_shown_preview_again click through columns to "Project Atlas.txt" and reread its pane; behaviour change 9 here goes away with your change.
- thumbnail-memory: (a) the Images row of the manual's preview table now ends "An image that fffinder draws itself isn't read again when its file changes: it keeps the look it first had, even after Refresh, until fffinder is started again." Your change makes that false: drop it in favour of your own sentence. The last clause of this change's changelog entry ("and a picture still shows as it was first drawn until fffinder is restarted") goes the same way when the changelog is assembled. (b) `previews` and `preview_tasks` changed type on the two lines above your `preview_images` field. (c) Your key is the path and the date of the entry `preview_body` is given, which is the row's: that is the rule the stamp follows, and a reread now asks for the selected item's preview again, so an image follows its row like everything else. With the same date (a file written over in place and dated back) Refresh reads a text again and not your image; the manual's new paragraph says Refresh reads the shown item's preview again whatever its size and date say.
- image-preview-details, preview-card-height, table-preview-column-widths: `previews` holds `(PreviewStamp, Preview)`; read it through `preview_of`. Whatever a `Preview` carries (pixel dimensions, say) is read again when the row's stamp changes, and the old value shows until then. Always give `ensure_preview` the row's own entry: an entry from a fresh stat, alternating with the row's, starts a load at every ask, which in the gallery is every frame. The new tests in tests/basics.rs stand after the_preview_pane_follows_the_selection and after a_preview_marks_no_line_when_the_file_changed_after_the_search.
- preview-page-keys: `ensure_pdf` is now reached at every reread while Quick Look is open, through `selection_changed`, and does nothing unless the row's date changed. quick_look_opens_a_pdf_again_once_it_has_changed presses Page Down in Quick Look's own window and reads `shown_pdf_page()`; your routers have to keep that key paging there.
- quick-look-empty-state: with nothing selected `selection_changed` does nothing, at a reread as before. Empty the cache with `forget_previews(cx)`, which also drops the loads and asks again.
- view-switch-keeps-selection: after your helper selects in pane 0, `set_view_mode`'s `selection_changed` asks with the same entry (pane 0's entries are the rows') and starts nothing more.
- stale-rows-on-place-change, files-changed-off-thread: `load_listing`'s completion always calls `selection_changed` now. If you replace `results` or patch rows somewhere else, call it there too, and build the entries as the rows had them (a search by name has the index's size and date) or the preview is read once more.
- restore-session-tabs: each tab looks every two seconds whether it shows or not, and now reads its selected item's preview again when that item changed. A tab restored with nothing selected reads none.
- select-all-perf: `selection_changed` runs at every reread now and costs `primary_entry()`; keep that from walking the selection.
- filter-stale-keep-set: `nu_changed` calls `forget_previews(cx)` where it cleared the two maps and called `selection_changed`.
- content-match-highlight: when a contents search runs again, the old text shows against the new hit until the file is read again; `hit_range` marks nothing in between unless the line still reads the same.

Found, not fixed (on the trunk before this change, outside this brief; the first five are the implementer's, which I read or saw again).
- Column view with Quick Look open: clicking a folder in the browser leaves Quick Look on a spinner. `select_in_column` asks for no preview for a folder and never calls `selection_changed`; a clicked PDF or structured file gets its preview but no `ensure_pdf` or `ensure_explore`. The arrow keys in Quick Look do all three. lane-f is splitting that function.
- Pictures aren't read again (see left_out); thumbnail-memory has it.
- A folder's item count follows the folder's row, which is read again only when the folder's parent changes.
- In the results of a search by name a file changed in place keeps the index's size and date, so its preview isn't read again until the search's rows change.
- Refresh in the gallery can read a changed file twice.
- A `nu` started for a preview or for explore mode can't be stopped: dropping the task stops the waiting, and the process runs to its end or its 10-second timeout.
- Explore mode shows its loading state each time the file's date changes, where a preview keeps the old one up.
